\section{Invariants and Derivations (hand-curated)}

\subsection{The mount predicate}

Let $p$ be a candidate plugin. Four independent predicates gate it:

\begin{align}
  \mathrm{disc}(p)  &\iff \exists\, \texttt{plugin.toml} \in \mathrm{root}(p)
                       \;\wedge\; \mathrm{kind}(p) = \texttt{config-renderer}
                       \label{lbl:disc}\\
  \mathrm{det}(p)   &\iff \mathrm{disc}(p) \wedge \mathrm{exists}\!\left(\mathrm{requires\_path}(p)\right)
                       \label{lbl:det}\\
  \mathrm{reg}(p)   &\iff \exists\, [[\texttt{tool}]] \in R \;\wedge\; \mathrm{enabled}(p) = \top
                       \label{lbl:reg}\\
  \mathrm{gate}(p)  &\iff \texttt{is\_enabled}(p) = \top
                       \label{lbl:gate}
\end{align}

The mount decision is their conjunction:

\begin{equation}
  \boxed{\;\mathrm{mounted}(p) \iff
    \mathrm{disc}(p) \wedge \mathrm{det}(p) \wedge \mathrm{reg}(p) \wedge \mathrm{gate}(p)\;}
  \label{lbl:mounted}
\end{equation}

\noindent
where $R$ is the registry \texttt{\textasciitilde/.config/beagle/plugins/tools.toml}.

\paragraph{Detection is not activation.}
Equation~\eqref{lbl:mounted} is a conjunction, not an implication, which is precisely
the Skylon semantics: $\mathrm{det}(p) \not\Rightarrow \mathrm{mounted}(p)$. A plugin whose
host is present but which is unlisted in $R$ is \emph{gated} --- reported by
\texttt{plugin\_status} and never mounted. This is rule~\texttt{PLG-5}: enlarging the
mounted set requires editing $R$, never engine code.

\paragraph{Inertness under an absent host.}
If $\neg\,\mathrm{exists}(\mathrm{requires\_path}(p))$ then $\neg\,\mathrm{det}(p)$, so by
\eqref{lbl:mounted} $p$ is not mounted, and by~\texttt{PLG-1} the correct observable state
is \emph{inert}, not \emph{errored}:
\begin{equation}
  \neg\,\mathrm{det}(p) \;\Rightarrow\; \mathrm{state}(p) = \texttt{inert}
  \;\wedge\; \mathrm{error}(p) = \varnothing .
  \label{lbl:inert}
\end{equation}

\subsection{Detachability}

Let $G$ be the guide source directory, supplied by configuration rather than by code.
Write $\rho_{p}(G)$ for the render of plugin $p$ against $G$. Rule~\texttt{PLG-2} demands

\begin{equation}
  \forall G' \text{ well-formed}: \quad \rho_{p}(G') \text{ is defined},
  \label{lbl:detach}
\end{equation}

so no particular provider --- Beagle included --- appears in the domain condition.
Beagle is the \emph{default} value of $G$, never a precondition of $\rho_p$.

\subsection{Idempotence and region isolation}

Let $F$ be the output file, partitioned by the marker pair into a generated region
$F_{\mathrm{gen}}$ and its complement $F_{\mathrm{hand}}$, with $F = F_{\mathrm{hand}} \sqcup F_{\mathrm{gen}}$.
Rules~\texttt{PLG-3} and~\texttt{PLG-4} give

\begin{align}
  \rho_p\!\left(\rho_p(F)\right) &= \rho_p(F)
    &&\text{(idempotence)} \label{lbl:idem}\\
  \pi_{\mathrm{hand}}\!\left(\rho_p(F)\right) &= \pi_{\mathrm{hand}}(F)
    &&\text{(hand-authored text is invariant)} \label{lbl:iso}
\end{align}

Drift is detectable without re-rendering, because the region records
$h = \mathrm{sha256}_{\mathrm{c14n}}(T)$ of its source guide $T$; the output is stale iff

\begin{equation}
  h_{\text{recorded}} \neq \mathrm{sha256}_{\mathrm{c14n}}(T_{\text{current}}).
  \label{lbl:drift}
\end{equation}

Canonical form is sorted-key JSON, so key reordering in $T$ does not churn $h$.
